text: THE COLORDISK Version 2.0 Use this disk to estimate the saturation cost of mixing two paint pigments. Paint mixing paths generally curve. Paths connecting CMY pigments curve outward; paths connecting SGI curve inward; paths through the green sector curve outward. The center of the disk represents D65, a standard achromatic point in colorimetry. Chroma increases from this central point outward. Visually complementary hues are opposite each other. The vertical axis divides the warm and cool hues. CIECAM02 opponent axes (a* and b*) are labeled. A number of pigment Color Index codes are mapped according to Bruce McEvoyʼs spectrophotometer readings, with the black outline approximating the pigment gamut. The white outline approximates the sRGB gamut. Besides using this disk as a reference for complementary pairs, estimating saturation cost, etc., you can use this disk for gamut masking (a method for creating harmonious palettes described by James Gurney). Finally, you can use the disk as a color isolator by punching a view-hole through the center; the innermost 1” diameter circle is neutral gray. Y I M C G S By Peter T.
